author: Admilson B. F. Cossa
authority: runtime source and npm run verify

claims.title: run.race cancels losing branches
claims.expectedInvariant: losing branches receive race_lost cancellation
claims.limitations: Provider billing or remote execution stops only when the underlying provider honors AbortSignal.

claims.title: run.retry stops on parent cancellation
claims.expectedInvariant: no extra retry attempt runs after cancellation is observed
claims.limitations: The guarantee applies to WorkIt retry sleeps and task bodies that observe ctx.signal.

claims.title: run.bracket cleanup timeout is bounded and observable
claims.expectedInvariant: a hanging cleanup emits task:cleanup_timeout and the owner settles
claims.limitations: The timeout bounds WorkIt cleanup waiting; external systems still need their own timeout and idempotency policies.

claims.title: replay receipts record completed scope closure
claims.expectedInvariant: a closed successful scope has completed terminal outcome and no leaked tasks
claims.limitations: Receipts are audit evidence over observed WorkIt events and snapshots; they are not deterministic scheduler replay.

claims.title: replay receipts preserve typed cancellation reason
claims.expectedInvariant: a manually cancelled scope records the cancellation reason observed by owned work
claims.limitations: The reason is evidence captured from WorkIt-owned cancellation; external systems still need their own abort support.

claims.title: shared scope resource acquires and releases once
claims.expectedInvariant: parallel tasks using one shared helper observe one acquisition and one scope-owned release
claims.limitations: This proves WorkIt helper ownership and cleanup registration; external resource semantics remain application responsibility.

claims.title: file activity store replays completed activity after restart
claims.expectedInvariant: a fresh file activity store returns the persisted terminal result without rerunning the activity body
claims.limitations: This is terminal activity replay for explicit activity ids; it is not arbitrary in-flight crash recovery or workflow replay.

claims.title: resource cleanup audit records success, failure, and timeout paths
claims.expectedInvariant: resource audit instrumentation records acquired/released/pending resources while WorkIt emits cleanup timeout and failure events
claims.limitations: Successful resource acquisition and release entries are explicit audit instrumentation in the evidence harness. WorkIt's current first-class event surface exposes cleanup failures and timeouts, not every successful cleanup start/completion.

claims.title: attempt evidence records admitted retry invocations
claims.expectedInvariant: each admitted invocation records its attempt number and outcome while bounded metadata applies default secret redaction
claims.limitations: Attempt recording wraps explicit task bodies. It does not infer provider policy, prove remote cancellation, or provide deterministic scheduler replay.

claims.title: candidate deadline is aggregate and terminal across the chain
claims.expectedInvariant: one absolute deadline reaches the admitted candidate context and timeout admits no fallback candidate
claims.limitations: Timer precision depends on the JavaScript event loop, and remote providers stop only when they honor AbortSignal.

claims.title: candidate callback cancellation remains authoritative
claims.expectedInvariant: cancellation thrown by quality or classification callbacks propagates unchanged and admits no fallback
claims.limitations: The proof covers typed in-process WorkIt cancellation, not provider-side termination without cooperative AbortSignal support.

claims.title: budget inputs are immutable boundary values
claims.expectedInvariant: caller input object is not mutated; final spent value is read from run.context.budget
claims.limitations: Applications must read runtime budget state through the context API rather than expecting mutation of the original object.

claims.title: channel capacity applies producer backpressure
claims.expectedInvariant: third send to capacity-two channel blocks until a receive drains one item
claims.limitations: This proof covers local channel capacity, not distributed queue semantics.

claims.title: diagnostics report stable cleanup finding codes
claims.expectedInvariant: cleanup timeout events produce cleanup_timeout findings
claims.limitations: Rich rendering and exporter behavior are separate optional surfaces.

claims.title: retry policy rejects unsafe attempt counts
claims.expectedInvariant: unbounded retry counts are rejected at the policy boundary
claims.limitations: The cap prevents accidental huge retry policies; application-level retry budgets may be stricter.

claims.title: agent authority denies undeclared capability before tool execution
claims.expectedInvariant: denied declared tool capability emits agent:tool_denied and the tool body is never called
claims.limitations: This is declared tool policy inside runAgent, not operating-system, filesystem, network, or CPU sandboxing.

claims.title: receipt analysis detects leaked owned work
claims.expectedInvariant: a non-terminal receipt with pending tasks fails analysis with leaked_tasks
claims.limitations: The verifier analyzes receipt evidence supplied to it; it does not observe work that was never captured.

claims.title: time-policy planner computes retry upper bounds
claims.expectedInvariant: retry upper bound includes attempt duration and delays between failed attempts only
claims.limitations: The planner computes declared policy bounds before execution; it does not run user task bodies.

claims.title: time-policy planner reports infeasible deadline
claims.expectedInvariant: deadline planning returns invalid before runtime execution when policy cannot fit
claims.limitations: Deadline feasibility is computed from the supplied clock and policy; applications remain responsible for accurate external deadlines.

claims.title: fault injection harness records lifecycle evidence through real scopes
claims.expectedInvariant: bounded cancellation, cleanup timeout, provider timeout, and retry exhaustion scenarios return passing reports with WorkIt receipts
claims.limitations: This is bounded in-process fault injection through explicit scenarios; it is not deterministic replay, SIGKILL recovery, or an operating-system fault injector.

claims.title: explicit activity boundary preserves terminal evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: completed activity returns the stored result on repeat and changed input conflicts before rerun
claims.limitations: The boundary records explicit terminal activity evidence; callers remain responsible for idempotent external side effects.

claims.title: receipt verifier proves declared lifecycle evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: a closed receipt with terminal and cleanup evidence verifies no orphaned owned tasks while preserving cleanup timeout warning evidence
claims.limitations: Verification is bounded to the receipt and snapshot supplied by the caller.

claims.title: bounded resource model preserves cleanup balance invariant
claims.expectedInvariant: for linear, lazy, and shared resources, every terminal modeled scope releases exactly the resources it acquired
claims.limitations: This is a bounded model for WorkIt resource helper contracts, not a proof over arbitrary JavaScript programs or external resources.

claims.title: bounded time-policy model preserves cost upper-bound invariant
claims.expectedInvariant: for generated bounded policies, planTimePolicy returns an upper bound that dominates the modeled critical path cost
claims.limitations: This is a bounded executable model for WorkIt time-policy planning, not a proof over arbitrary JavaScript, wall-clock scheduling, timer precision, event-loop stalls, provider behavior, jitter, or dynamic backoff functions.

claims.title: source protocol analysis detects missing ownership edges
claims.expectedInvariant: bounded source protocol specs pass when WorkIt ownership edges are present and fail with stable findings when ownership edges are missing
claims.limitations: This verifies caller-provided protocol specifications, not arbitrary TypeScript or JavaScript source.

claims.title: nested time-policy planner preserves recursive composition bounds
claims.expectedInvariant: generated nested policies match the recursive model for upper bounds, attempts, parallel work, truncation limits, and typed timeout/deadline warnings
claims.limitations: This is a bounded executable proof over generated nested policy trees. It is not a theorem over arbitrary TypeScript programs, wall-clock scheduling, provider latency, or completed mechanized proof.

claims.title: typed cancellation contracts reject undeclared task composition
claims.expectedInvariant: tsc accepts declared cancellable/shielded composition and rejects plain or misrouted tasks
claims.limitations: This proves an optional compile-time intent contract at the contracts subpath. It does not prove that arbitrary task bodies observe ctx.signal or change the root WorkIt API.

claims.title: task context exposes the effective composed deadline
claims.expectedInvariant: nested retry and fallback attempts observe the absolute deadline declared by the owning wrapper
claims.limitations: Deadline introspection reports runtime policy. Timer precision and task termination still depend on the event loop and cooperative AbortSignal handling.

claims.title: shared retry budget blocks excess attempts before execution
claims.expectedInvariant: retry wrappers sharing one scope budget cannot execute a retry after the aggregate budget is exhausted
claims.limitations: The budget counts retries admitted by WorkIt wrappers. External provider attempts outside the wrapped task remain application responsibility.

claims.title: deadline retry fallback cancellation and receipt evidence compose
claims.expectedInvariant: a cancelled retry/fallback composition preserves its effective deadline and records each admitted attempt in its terminal receipt
claims.limitations: The proof exercises cooperative in-process cancellation. It does not prove provider cancellation or wall-clock scheduler precision.

claims.title: time-policy planner aggregates shared retry budget demand
claims.expectedInvariant: nested retry policies referencing one budget key are inadmissible when aggregate demand exceeds the supplied runtime budget snapshot
claims.limitations: Planning uses an explicit point-in-time budget snapshot. Concurrent runtime consumption after planning can reduce the remaining budget before execution.

claims.title: candidate policy separates retries, quality rejection, and fallback
claims.expectedInvariant: a retryable transport failure, successful low-quality result, and accepted fallback produce distinct ordered bounded evidence
claims.limitations: Candidate execution is sequential and in-process. Provider side effects remain caller-owned and require caller-supplied idempotency.

claims.title: candidate policy preserves authoritative cancellation
claims.expectedInvariant: a real WorkIt cancellation bypasses provider classification and admits no later candidate
claims.limitations: Remote work stops only when the underlying provider cooperates with AbortSignal.

claims.title: candidate retries share the WorkIt retry budget
claims.expectedInvariant: candidate fallback cannot admit a retry after the shared scope retry budget is exhausted
claims.limitations: The budget covers retries admitted by WorkIt. Calls performed outside the candidate task remain application responsibility.

claims.title: candidate admission and aggregate attempts are bounded
claims.expectedInvariant: callbacks cannot expand the admitted candidate snapshot and unsafe candidate-count by retry-count products fail before execution
claims.limitations: The configured maximum bounds WorkIt admissions; it does not account for provider-internal retries outside the candidate task.

claims.title: candidate decisions are normalized exactly once
claims.expectedInvariant: mutable getters cannot change failure disposition, reason, or acceptance after validation
claims.limitations: Normalization protects WorkIt policy reads; callers still own mutable candidate and result objects passed to their callbacks.

claims.title: candidate error taxonomy is conservative and provider-neutral
claims.expectedInvariant: known WorkIt cancellation, timeout, and budget failures have stable decisions while unknown provider errors remain unclassified
claims.limitations: Provider-specific errors require a caller classifier; WorkIt does not infer HTTP, SDK, billing, or safety policy.

claims.title: candidate callback failures do not become fallback
claims.expectedInvariant: quality and classifier callback bugs propagate unchanged and admit no later candidate
claims.limitations: Applications remain responsible for testing their classifier and quality predicate implementations.

claims.title: telemetry context and observer failures remain isolated
claims.expectedInvariant: throwing telemetry context access and observers cannot escape event emission or block another observer
claims.limitations: Observer exceptions are intentionally discarded. Exporter diagnostics and delivery guarantees belong to opt-in observability adapters.
claims.ledgerNote: Backfilled after the 0.5.0 tag because its changelog claim had unit coverage but no dedicated claim-ledger entry.

claims.title: hostile thrown values cannot bypass candidate classification
claims.expectedInvariant: proxy traps and throwing Error accessors remain bounded while the caller classifier retains policy authority
claims.limitations: This is JavaScript object hardening, not isolation from arbitrary code executing in the same process.

claims.title: bounded operational candidate scenarios preserve declared policy
claims.expectedInvariant: quality fallback, caller-owned idempotency, user-input stops, and cooperative cancellation preserve their declared boundaries
claims.limitations: These are bounded in-process fixtures, not a real provider, durable-store, distributed-system, or Oryn production canary.

claims.title: worker offload rejects remote and executable URL schemes
claims.expectedInvariant: data, http, https, and javascript worker inputs are rejected before import
claims.limitations: Local file URLs remain application authority; WorkIt does not sandbox arbitrary trusted local code.

claims.title: worker timeout terminates non-cooperative CPU work
claims.expectedInvariant: late marker is not written after offload timeout
claims.limitations: The hard boundary applies to worker offload; JavaScript cannot preempt a CPU loop on the main thread.

claims.title: candidate metadata normalization keeps prototype-shaped fields inert
claims.expectedInvariant: an own __proto__ metadata field is retained as data without changing Object.prototype and secret fields are redacted
claims.limitations: This proof covers candidate evidence normalization. It is not a general object sandbox or protection for caller code that mutates global prototypes.

claims.title: public proof artifact exposes release evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/public-proof.json exposes commands, fixtures, guides, and runtime matrix
claims.limitations: This verifies repository artifact shape, not an external registry publication event.

claims.title: release policy documents signed tags and worker boundary
claims.expectedInvariant: SECURITY.md documents signed tags and structured-clone worker input
claims.limitations: Documentation must remain aligned with the actual release workflow.

claims.title: release provenance gate verifies tag policy
claims.expectedInvariant: release-provenance script contains signed-tag verification logic
claims.limitations: A dry-run gate cannot guarantee a future maintainer will sign a tag; it verifies that the repository policy gate exists.

claims.title: file receipt ledger persists append-only receipt evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: a receipt appended by one ledger instance is readable from a new ledger instance
claims.limitations: This proof covers WorkIt's file-backed receipt ledger, not database durability or distributed queue semantics.

claims.title: SQL receipt ledger adapters preserve idempotency and conflict detection
claims.expectedInvariant: SQLite and Postgres ledger ports return the same record for identical appends and reject conflicting receipt content
claims.limitations: The adapters use caller-owned database clients and validate their SQL identifier input; deployment-level durability, replication, backup, and transaction policy remain database responsibilities.

claims.title: SQLite receipt ledger persists through a real file-backed database
claims.expectedInvariant: a receipt appended through node:sqlite is readable after database close and reopen, while conflicting content is rejected
claims.limitations: This proof uses node:sqlite when the active Node runtime provides it. Postgres remains an environment-gated integration path because WorkIt does not take a runtime pg dependency.

claims.title: candidates subpath has locked ESM CommonJS and type artifacts
claims.expectedInvariant: dedicated ESM, CommonJS, and declaration artifacts expose firstAcceptable while the root API remains unchanged
claims.limitations: Installed-tarball and runtime-matrix behavior is verified by the separate package-consumer release gate.

claims.title: published core has zero runtime dependencies
claims.expectedInvariant: package dependencies are absent and the generated CycloneDX SBOM contains no runtime components
claims.limitations: Development and optional peer dependencies remain outside the zero-runtime-dependency claim.
claims.ledgerNote: Backfilled after the 0.5.0 tag because the release changelog claim was enforced by SBOM gates but absent from the claim ledger.

claims.title: compiled package entrypoints stay within enforced size budgets
claims.expectedInvariant: the size gate passes for compiled root, group, candidates ESM, and candidates CommonJS artifacts
claims.limitations: Bundle results depend on the pinned build toolchain and measure declared fixtures rather than every consumer bundler configuration.
claims.ledgerNote: The root and group measurements backfill the 0.5.0 claim; candidate measurements apply to the 0.6.0 target.

claims.title: Oryn real integration canary gates the 0.6.0 publication
claims.expectedInvariant: Oryn exercises firstAcceptable against its real provider boundary and caller-owned durable idempotency, preserving quality fallback, retry budget, aggregate deadline, cancellation, user-input stop, and bounded redacted evidence before v0.6.0 is tagged
claims.limitations: One local Oryn edge/daemon canary crossed real Ollama provider and daemon receipt boundaries. It is not a production-load, multi-host, or long-duration soak result; retry-budget, deadline, and requires-user-input faults remain controlled boundary scenarios.
claims.ledgerNote: Resolved by the redacted receipt in evidence/oryn-candidate-canary.v0.6.0.json, bound to WorkIt commit 077b5b1, Oryn commit 2e8c7b2, and the packed tarball SHA-256.

claims.title: 0.6.1 locks declarations compatibility and reproducible packaging
claims.expectedInvariant: declarations and 0.6.0 compatibility are locked, Node 20.11/22/24 are exercised, two builds pack identically, public benchmark thresholds drive their gates, and 1,000 runs per property are scheduled nightly with rotating reproducible seeds
claims.limitations: The declaration snapshot intentionally freezes the complete generated type graph. The Node matrix and deep property profile execute in CI; local release verification covers the active Node version and bounded property profile unless explicitly overridden.

claims.title: Oryn real integration canary gates the 0.6.1 publication
claims.expectedInvariant: Oryn exercises the packed 0.6.1 artifact against its real provider and daemon boundaries while preserving quality fallback, durable replay, retry budget, aggregate deadline, user-input stop, and bounded redacted evidence
claims.limitations: One local Oryn edge/daemon canary crossed real Ollama provider and daemon receipt boundaries. It is not a production-load, multi-host, or long-duration soak result; retry-budget, deadline, and requires-user-input faults remain controlled boundary scenarios.
claims.ledgerNote: Resolved by the redacted receipt in evidence/oryn-hardening-canary.v0.6.1.json, bound to WorkIt commit eec670d, Oryn base commit 2e8c7b2, the canary dependency files, script, and packed tarball SHA-256.

claims.title: article benchmark suite has expected executable coverage
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/articles contains exactly 19 numbered benchmark scripts
claims.limitations: Coverage count does not prove a benchmark result; individual benchmark assertions do.

claims.title: captured article benchmark result is machine-readable
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/results/articles.latest.json records 19 passing benches
claims.limitations: Timing values are representative for the captured machine and run; semantic assertions are the portable claim.

claims.title: candidate execution and retained evidence remain bounded
claims.expectedInvariant: large quality and retry chains stay inside time and retained-heap budgets while evidence retains only its configured window
claims.limitations: Timings and heap deltas are environment-sensitive regression bounds, not universal latency or memory guarantees.

claims.title: scope idempotency is not durable idempotency
claims.expectedInvariant: TaskOpts.idempotencyKey is documented as live-scope coalescing and durable restart behavior remains caller-owned
claims.limitations: Applications requiring restart-safe side effects must use a durable idempotency store or an explicit activity boundary.
claims.ledgerNote: Backfilled after the 0.5.0 tag as an explicit product-decision claim.

claims.title: candidate side-effect idempotency remains caller-owned
claims.expectedInvariant: firstAcceptable remains a sequential in-process policy helper and does not imply durable idempotency or background handoff
claims.limitations: Retries and fallback can repeat side effects; callers must supply durable idempotency where operations are not naturally safe.
